TC-BUY-001.actual: Step 1 (name, email, phone, password) and step 2 (photo, birthday, sex, address, government ID) were accepted with no errors. An "Account Submitted!" message said the account is being reviewed by the team. The account was saved as a buyer with application status "pending" (phone stored as +639171234567). Emails sent: "Welcome to Loved-IT!". No OTP was sent and no email verification page opened.
TC-BUY-001.remarks: Design difference (A9, A12): the system verifies new buyers by an admin review of their government ID, not by an email OTP. The phone was typed as 9171234567 after the fixed +63 prefix. Test data emails use @example.com, which the system rejects (its email check needs a domain that accepts mail; example.com has a null MX), so the same address was used with @gmail.com. Mail went to the isolated test log only. Screenshot: TC-BUY-001.jpg Recovered evidence from the prior recorded browser run; reviewed in this continuation, not rerun as a fresh account test.

TC-BUY-002.remarks: Registration is blocked, but a message appears for one field at a time, not for every mandatory field at once, and the phone field has no required marker for the browser. TC-BUY-014.actual: 10 digits "0917123456": accepted and saved as +630917123456; 11 digits "09170000001": accepted and saved as +630917000000; 12 digits "091712345678": rejected ("The phone has already been taken.").

TC-BUY-013.remarks: Defect: letters and symbols are silently removed and the remaining digits are put after +63, so invalid and landline numbers are saved without any message.
